newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Irish PM sees no fallout if Sweden shuns ERM.
newsitem.headline: Irish PM sees no fallout if Sweden shuns ERM.

text.p: Irish Prime Minister John Bruton said on Tuesday it would be preferable if Sweden entered Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM), but his personal view was that it might qualify anyway for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) starting 1999.

Bruton was in Sweden for talks with Prime Minister Goran Persson ahead of a European Union summit next month which Bruton will chair at the end of Ireland's six-month presidency of the EU Council of Ministers.

Asked at a news conference whether Sweden could do so without first entering the ERM, Bruton said "I would imagine without any authority of office that if Sweden wanted to enter the (single currency) euro in 1998, and economic fundamentals are on track, I don't think there would be a problem."
Bruton emphasised that his views were those of "an intelligent layman".

The Irish premier, who is touring European capitals before the Dublin summit, said he believed it could achieve agreement on a successor to the current ERM, and on an EU budget stability pact on December 13 and 14.
The new exchange rate mechanism, ERM2, would link the single-currency euro with currencies outside it.
"I think we will reach a decision on ERM2, and also the stability pact, though that is perhaps not so urgent. It would be preferable if we can keep up the momentum in Dublin," Bruton said.
There were still some differences among EU members over what constituted "temporary divergence" from the strict definitions of economic stability in EMU, he said.
Bruton said Sweden's continued absence from the ERM should not reduce its influence on employment and environmental questions, two questions close to Swedish hearts.
"I do not think there is any connection between the two issues," Bruton said. "It is not only Sweden that wants an employment chapter in a European treaty."
Noting Sweden's progress this year in reducing indebtedness and inflation and its sound economic fundamentals, Bruton said "That gives Sweden the choice to participate in the euro if it wants to."
